title: Your evening routine
hook: assemble: bell, breath, arti, one line

segments.voice: Yesterday, surya, the sun: just him, and you facing it. Your line was the original flame.

The phone falls on your face at midnight. Most days don't end. They just stop. Last week you built a morning. This week you've gathered the other end of the day, piece by piece. Sandhya, the hour where day and night join. Arti at home, a small flame circled. Om jai jagadish hare, the song everyone knows. Taking the light, hands over the flame to your eyes. Family arti, one more person in the room. And yesterday, the sun itself. Today they become the other bookend: your evening routine.
screen: `MOST DAYS DON'T END, THEY STOP.` → `A WEEK OF DUSK.` → `TODAY: THE OTHER BOOKEND.`

segments.voice: Here's a shape: four pieces, about five minutes, built only from things you already know. First, the bell. One ring, followed all the way to silence: arriving, from day one hundred fourteen. Second, the breath you learned back in week fifteen: in for four, out for six. A few rounds of the longer out-breath tell the body the day is closing. Third, arti. If you have a lamp, light it and circle it slowly, maybe humming the first line of the song. If you don't, face the window, toward where the sun went down. Then take the light: hands over the flame, back to your eyes. And fourth, one line. Many Hindu prayers close the same way, with Om and three shantis: Om shanti, shanti, shanti. Your fourth word, peace, peace, peace. Some people use their own mantra here instead. Just one line, said slowly, as the last thing. Bell, breath, arti, one line. Now notice what it's for. The morning puja offers the day before it starts. The evening routine hands the day back. Whatever happened, the good meeting, the argument, the thing you forgot, you don't have to carry it into sleep. People in many traditions have a way of closing the day. This is one Hindu way: a flame, a breath, a word of peace, and the day put down.
screen: `THE BELL: ARRIVE.` · `THE BREATH: LONGER OUT.` · `ARTI: THE FLAME, OR THE WINDOW.` · `ONE LINE: OM SHANTI, SHANTI, SHANTI.`

segments.voice: Ring your bell or tap a glass and follow the sound to silence, then breathe in for four and out for six, three times. If you have a flame, circle it slowly clockwise and take the light to your eyes, or if not, turn toward the window; then, quietly, if you'd like: Om shanti, shanti, shanti. Last, name one thing from today, just one, and set it down.
Dinacharya, the course of the day: bell, breath, arti, one line, five minutes that close it instead of letting it just stop. Today's word.
Your line: the day put down. Even a shortened version of the four pieces closes it. That's the week, and day one hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Many Hindu households close the day with evening arti at the home shrine, often with a bell, the circled lamp, a song or mantra, and a closing invocation of peace such as Om shanti shanti shanti.
